subject: Segmented invoicing buckets and contingent credit agreement
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@mediflow.com>
To: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Sabrina Lee <sabrina.lee@mediflow.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Segmented invoicing request + credit ceiling

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the trial run with Redwood — the team is impressed with throughput and the latency profile. Procurement is moving this forward but they need a billing approach that aligns with our release cadence. Two asks from our side: 

1) Segmented invoices: We prefer milestone invoices (integration & launch milestones) on Net30, and ongoing consumption invoices on Net60. Can Redwood produce separate invoices for milestones vs consumption, or would you prefer consolidated monthly statements with line-level payment terms?

2) Credit ceiling: We can sign a 12-month contract but need a provisional credit limit of $150,000 to cover expected consumption for Q1. If you require underwriting, we can share last 3 months of statements and a PO.

Also, important for our tax team: VAT needs to be invoiced to our EU entity (MediFlow GmbH, DE VAT DE123456789). Can Redwood support VAT-pass-through with separate entity invoicing?

I attached the draft PO so you can see expected volumes.

Next steps: We'd like a short mutual-action plan and any credit prescriptive terms you need.

Best,
Oliver
Head of Procurement
MediFlow Health

Attachment: MediFlow_PO_2026Q4.pdf (application/pdf, 98 KB)

From: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@mediflow.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-12-01T09:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Segmented invoicing request + credit ceiling

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the PO. Glad the trial performed well. Below is a proposed approach that balances MediFlow's procurement constraints with Redwood's billing controls: 

Proposal (high level):
- Segmented invoices: We can issue separate invoice buckets: (A) Milestone invoices (integration/launch) — Net30; (B) Consumption invoices — Net45 by default. If you need Net60 specifically for consumption we can consider it with a contingent credit addendum (see below).
- Contingent credit agreement: To support a Net60 on consumption and a $150k ceiling we would require either (i) a refundable security deposit of $25,000 posted up front, or (ii) a rolling prepay of month 1 consumption, combined with an approved credit application. The security deposit lets us extend Net60 while preserving internal credit exposure.
- Early-pay incentive: If you can pay consumption invoices within 15 days we can offer a 2% early-payment discount on those invoices (applies to consumption bucket only).
- VAT routing: We can route VAT invoices to MediFlow GmbH (DE VAT ID) — Finance will need the EU entity billing contact and exact invoicing address. For cross-entity arrangements we typically include a short Annex that confirms tax-responsibility and the invoice entity.

Attachments: I uploaded a short spreadsheet that maps the two invoice buckets and the initial credit addendum we would circulate for signature.

Next steps: 1) Please confirm whether you prefer Net45 or Net60 for consumption given the options above. 2) If Net60, confirm whether you'll provide the deposit or opt for rolling prepay + credit review. Once agreed we'll route the contingent credit addendum to DocuSign and copy Finance for the VAT entity paperwork.

I'll also loop Finance (Kimberly) and Legal (Marissa) so they can surface any compliance or T&Cs flags.

Best regards,
Priyom Das
Solutions Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed_terms_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 12 KB)

From: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

Priyom / Marissa — quick internal note after reviewing the proposed approach: 

- I'm generally comfortable with issuing separate invoice buckets (milestone Net30 / consumption Net45 as default). For full Net60 we need the credit addendum + either the $25k security deposit or an approved credit application.
- Request Finance to run a soft credit check on MediFlow and approve the $150k ceiling if their current liabilities look clean. If credit check is marginal, require the deposit.
- VAT: We can route invoices to MediFlow GmbH, but Legal will want a short Annex confirming tax residency and the entity accepting liability — Marissa can draft.

Can you capture these items in the mutual-action plan and include a HubSpot task for Finance review? I put the deal id in the note for tracking: D-2026-0789.
